'''Securities Board of Nepal (SEBON)''' ({{langx|ne|नेपाल धितोपत्र बोर्ड|}}) is the regulator of securities market in Nepal. It was established on June 7, 1993, after the first amendment in the Securities Exchange Act 1983.<ref>{{Cite book| publisher = Ink Vault Publications| isbn = 979-8-3211-0094-3|  title = Getting Started With The Share Market In Nepal| date = 2024-03-27|url=https://www.google.co.jp/books/edition/Getting_Started_With_The_Share_Market_In/3v-p0AEACAAJ?hl=en}}</ref><ref>{{Citation | last = Koirala| first = Radhika| title = A study on development of capital market in Nepal (with reference to NEPSE & SEBON)| date = 2012}}</ref> It follows the rules laid out in the Securities Act, 2006.<ref>{{Citation | last = Shrestha| first = Rajani| title = Performance of Securities Board of Nepal SEBON on capital Market in Nepal| date = 2009}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Medhacorplaw |date=2025-07-15 |title=Securities Act, 2007 (2063) |url=https://medhacorplaw.com/securities-act-2007-2063/ |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=MedhaCorpLaw |language=en-US}}</ref> The organization has four departments: Regulation, Supervision, Commodity Market and Research, and Management and Legal. These departments look after eight divisions, each responsible for different parts of the securities market. Within these divisions, there are twenty smaller sections.<ref>{{Cite web| title = SEBON| access-date = 2024-03-25| url = https://www.sebon.gov.np/about-sebon}}</ref>

SEBON gets its operation cost from the government, fees charged for transactions on the [[Nepal Stock Exchange|stock exchange]], and fees for registering corporate securities. Other income comes from fees for registering and renewing stock exchanges and other market players, as well as money from its revolving fund.

==Merchant Bank==
The '''Securities Board of Nepal''' (SEBON) regulates merchant banks under the '''Securities Businessperson (Merchant Banker) Regulations, 2064 (2008)'''. These regulations define the scope, licensing, and operational standards for merchant banking activities. Nepal has 32 licensed merchant banks, with several more in the pipeline. Most are subsidiaries of [[List of banks in Nepal#Class A: Commercial banks|commercial banks]], though a few operate independently.
